subject: Maths
title: Year 9 Maths Exam 4
intro: Answer every question. Show your working in the working box: method marks are given even when the final answer is wrong. You may not use a calculator.

questions.q: Which is the solution of 5 − 2x > 11?
questions.ms: Answer: B: x < −3. B1. −2x > 6, dividing by −2 flips the sign.

questions.q: Expand and simplify (x − 4)2
questions.ms: Answer: C: x² − 8x + 16. B1.

questions.q: Solve x2 = 49
questions.ms: Answer: B: x = 7 or x = −7. B1.

questions.q:
n is an integer and −3 < 2n + 1 ≤ 9.
List all the possible values of n.
questions.hint: Type the values from smallest to largest, separated by commas, like -2,0,3
questions.ms: Answer: −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4. M1 for −2 < n ≤ 4 (or −4 < 2n ≤ 8). A1 for −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 and no extras.

questions.q:
x is an integer.
2x + 3 > 1 and 3x − 2 ≤ 10
List all the possible values of x.
questions.hint: Type the values from smallest to largest, separated by commas, like -2,0,3
questions.ms: Answer: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4. M1 for x > −1 and x ≤ 4. A1 for 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 only.

questions.q:
A taxi charges AED 12 plus AED 3 for every kilometre. Yahia has AED 50.
Write an inequality for the number of kilometres, k, that Yahia can travel.
questions.hint: Type it like x>4 or -2<x<=3 (use <= for ≤ and >= for ≥)
questions.ms: Answer: 12 + 3k ≤ 50. B1 for 12 + 3k ≤ 50 (accept 3k + 12 ≤ 50). Must be ≤, not =.

questions.q: Work out the greatest whole number of kilometres he can travel. (km)
questions.ms: Answer: 12 km. M1 for 3k ≤ 38 or k ≤ 12.66… A1 for 12 (not 13, not 12.7).

questions.q: Expand and simplify (x + 2)(x − 3)(x + 1)
questions.ms: Answer: x³ − 7x − 6. M1 for expanding one pair correctly, e.g. x² − x − 6. M1 for multiplying by the third bracket with at most one error (6 terms). A1 for x³ − 7x − 6.

questions.q: Factorise 3x2 + 10x − 8
questions.ms: Answer: (3x − 2)(x + 4). M1 for (3x ± 2)(x ± 4) or splitting 10x into 12x − 2x. A1 for (3x − 2)(x + 4).

questions.q: Factorise 6x2 − 11x + 3
questions.ms: Answer: (3x − 1)(2x − 3). M1 for brackets that give two of the three terms, or splitting −11x into −9x − 2x. A1 for (3x − 1)(2x − 3).

questions.q: Factorise fully 2x2 − 50
questions.ms: Answer: 2(x − 5)(x + 5). M1 for 2(x² − 25) or (2x − 10)(x + 5) etc. A1 for 2(x − 5)(x + 5).

questions.q: Solve 2x2 + 7x − 15 = 0 by factorising.
questions.hint: Type both answers separated by a comma, like 3,-2
questions.ms: Answer: x = 1.5 or x = −5 (from (2x − 3)(x + 5) = 0). M1 for (2x ± 3)(x ± 5). A1 for (2x − 3)(x + 5). A1 for x = 3/2 and x = −5.

questions.q:
Sam solves x(x − 4) = 3(x − 4).
He divides both sides by (x − 4) and writes x = 3.
Explain what is wrong with Sam's method.
questions.ms: Answer: Dividing by (x − 4) loses the solution x = 4 (you cannot divide by x − 4 when it could be 0).. B1 for saying dividing by (x − 4) loses a solution, or that x − 4 could be zero, or that x = 4 also works.

questions.q: Solve x(x − 4) = 3(x − 4) correctly. Give all the solutions.
questions.hint: Type both answers separated by a comma, like 3,-2
questions.ms: Answer: x = 3 or x = 4. M1 for (x − 4)(x − 3) = 0 or x² − 7x + 12 = 0. A1 for x = 3 and x = 4.

questions.q:
The curve y = x2 − 6x + 5 is drawn.
Find the x-coordinates where the curve crosses the x-axis.
questions.hint: Type both answers separated by a comma, like 3,-2
questions.ms: Answer: x = 1 and x = 5. M1 for (x − 1)(x − 5) = 0. A1 for 1 and 5.

questions.q: Write down the x-coordinate of the turning point.
questions.ms: Answer: x = 3. B1 for 3 (midway between 1 and 5).

questions.q: Find the minimum value of y.
questions.ms: Answer: y = −4. M1 for substituting x = 3: 9 − 18 + 5. A1 for −4.

questions.q:
A ball is thrown upwards. Its height, h metres, after t seconds is h = 20t − 5t2.
Find the two times when the ball is at ground level. (seconds)
questions.hint: Type both answers separated by a comma, like 3,-2
questions.ms: Answer: t = 0 and t = 4. M1 for 5t(4 − t) = 0. A1 for 0 and 4.

questions.q: Find the maximum height of the ball. (m)
questions.ms: Answer: 20 m (at t = 2). M1 for using t = 2 (midway between 0 and 4). A1 for 20.

questions.q: For how many seconds is the ball at least 15 m above the ground? (seconds)
questions.ms: Answer: 2 seconds (from t = 1 to t = 3). M1 for 20t − 5t² = 15 or t² − 4t + 3 = 0. M1 for t = 1 and t = 3. A1 for 2 seconds.

questions.q:
A rectangle is (x + 5) cm long and (x − 2) cm wide. Its area is 30 cm2.
Show that x2 + 3x − 40 = 0
questions.ms: Answer: (x + 5)(x − 2) = x² + 3x − 10 = 30, so x² + 3x − 40 = 0. M1 for (x + 5)(x − 2) = 30. A1 for expanding to x² + 3x − 10 = 30 and rearranging (show-that: every step needed).

questions.q: Solve x2 + 3x − 40 = 0 and hence find the length of the rectangle. (cm)
questions.ms: Answer: x = 5 (x = −8 rejected), so the length is 10 cm. M1 for (x + 8)(x − 5) = 0. A1 for x = 5 (rejecting −8 because the width would be negative). A1 for length 10 cm.

questions.q: Solve x2 − x − 12 < 0
questions.hint: Type it like x>4 or -2<x<=3 (use <= for ≤ and >= for ≥)
questions.ms: Answer: −3 < x < 4. M1 for (x − 4)(x + 3). M1 for critical values −3 and 4. A1 for −3 < x < 4.

questions.q: Prove that the sum of any three consecutive integers is always a multiple of 3.
questions.ms: Answer: n + (n + 1) + (n + 2) = 3n + 3 = 3(n + 1), which is a multiple of 3.. B1 for n, n + 1, n + 2. M1 for 3n + 3. A1 for 3(n + 1) with a statement that it is a multiple of 3.

questions.q: Prove that the difference between the squares of two consecutive odd numbers is always a multiple of 8.
questions.ms: Answer: (2n + 3)² − (2n + 1)² = 4n² + 12n + 9 − 4n² − 4n − 1 = 8n + 8 = 8(n + 1). B1 for two consecutive odd numbers written as 2n + 1 and 2n + 3. M1 for expanding both squares. A1 for 8n + 8. A1 for 8(n + 1) with a conclusion.
